chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sa'd ibn Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I judge among you based on proofs and oaths, and some of you are more eloquent in presenting their argument than others. So whoever I award a portion of his brother's wealth, I am merely giving him a piece of Hellfire.'
ai.seo_question: Why is a judge's ruling based on proofs considered potentially temporary or subject to divine reckoning?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi underscores the provisional nature of Islamic judicial rulings, where judges decide based on apparent evidence (zahir) rather than absolute truth. It highlights the risk of injustice when eloquence or strong oaths mislead the court, framing the awarded wealth not as a divine blessing but as a 'piece of Hellfire' if the underlying reality differs. This concept is central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of court decisions and the spiritual accountability of both the judge and the recipient.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, both together from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Sa’ad Bin Hisham Bin Al Hakam,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘But rather I<sup>saww</sup> judge among you with the proofs and the oath, and some of you are more mistaken in their arguments than the others. So whichever man I<sup>saww</sup> cut off for him, anything from the wealth of his brother, so rather I<sup>asws</sup> have cut-off for him, by it, a piece from the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Sa‘d ibn Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘I must judge among you on the basis of evidence and oath. Certain ones among you make more mistakes in their argument than others. For whomever I cut off (takes away) from the assets of his brother, I only cut off for him thereby a piece of the fire.’”
